t: #3575 Maximum Good Subtree Score — Bitmask Tree DP
o: For every node u we need the best sum of a node subset inside u's subtree such that no decimal digit appears twice across chosen values, then sum all n answers mod 1e9+7. There are only 10 digits, so a subset's digit usage is a 10-bit mask (1024 options). Classic tree knapsack: each node keeps a table mapping digit-mask → best sum, and we merge child tables with mask-OR convolution. Values are positive (≥1), so including the empty subset (value 0, mask 0) is safe and never harmful. n ≤ 500 keeps the O(edges · 1024²) merge cost acceptable in compiled languages.
k: Digit usage of any value fits a 10-bit mask; 'good' subsets are exactly mask-disjoint unions.
Tree knapsack: dp[u][mask] = best sum using nodes of subtree(u) whose combined digit mask is exactly mask.
Answer for u is max over all masks of dp[u][mask]; sum these mod 1e9+7.

a.n: Approach 1: Bottom-up tree knapsack on sparse mask dictionaries
a.i: Process nodes in reverse DFS preorder so children finish before parents. Each node starts with {(own mask): val, 0: 0}; merging a child tries all (parent-mask, child-mask) pairs and keeps the best sum for each OR'd mask. Sparse dictionaries skip unreachable masks, which keeps practical performance far below the worst case.
s: Build children lists and a DFS preorder from root 0.
Iterate nodes in reverse preorder; initialize the node's table with its own value's digit mask and the empty subset.
Merge each child's table via mask-OR addition, keeping maximum sums.
Add max(table values) per node to the answer modulo 1e9+7.
a.t: O(n · 1024²) worst case for the mask convolutions across all edges; sparse maps make it much faster in practice
a.sp: O(n · 1024) for the per-node tables in the worst case

w: Present the tree-knapsack framing first, then the sparse-map implementation. Watch for: par[i] not necessarily < i (so topological order must be computed, not assumed), recursion depth (use iterative DFS), and taking the modulo only at the very end per node (intermediate sums fit in 64-bit). Follow-ups: report the actual best subset per node (store parent pointers), or handle negative values (then the empty subset matters and pruning changes).
